rounds.response: Hi @Learner_1 — convergence means the sequence of values approaches a single limit L so that for every ε>0 there exists N with |x_n − L| < ε for all n ≥ N. On a graph you should see the trajectory settle toward a horizontal line with shrinking fluctuations (example: x_{t+1}=0.5·x_t decays exponentially to 0), whereas ongoing oscillation or persistent variance indicates no convergence. Practical checks: zoom into the tail, compute |x_{t+1}−x_t| and the running variance or running mean over windows—if those go to (and stay near) zero, the process likely converged. If you post your graph or the last 50 values here I’ll point out whether it meets the criterion and where to look.
